correctness.rationale: For fixed \(N\), equality of Shannon entropy is equivalent to equality of \(Q=\prod_i n_i^{n_i}\), while equality of Simpson concentration is equivalent to equality of \(\sum_i n_i^2\). Every positive-integer partition through \(N=30\) is exhaustively checked, and the independently computed partition counts match. The first pair and triple collisions are therefore complete finite classifications.

value.rationale: Richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson diversity are the canonical orders 0, 1, and 2 in the Hill framework. Determining when these summaries cease to recover the underlying integer abundance composition is a natural inverse problem. The sharp finite cutoffs and complete first collision layers give a useful exact benchmark for information loss in standard biodiversity summaries.
